chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is the parting of the hair from the Sunnah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' I said, 'So did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) part (his hair)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'How is it that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) parted (his hair) and it is not from the Sunnah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The one who is hit by what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was hit by, parts just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) parted, so he has attained the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); otherwise, no.'

I said to him, 'How is that?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was turned away from the House (the Kaaba), and he had brought the sacrificial animal and was in Ihram, Allah showed him the vision which Allah had informed him of in His Book, when He says: "Certainly Allah had endorsed to His Messenger the vision with the truth: You shall enter the Sacred Masjid, if Allah Pleases, in security, having your heads shaved and having your hair cut, you shall not be fearing."'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) knew that Allah would fulfill for him what He had shown him. From then on, he preserved the hair that was on his head when he was in Ihram, awaiting its shaving in the Sanctuary, where Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had promised him. So when he shaved it, he did not repeat the preservation of the hair, nor was that (preservation) from before him (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: Ihram (ritual state for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَا: Vision (specifically the vision of entering Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Is parting the hair during Ihram considered Sunnah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the distinction between general Sunnah and specific prophetic precedent (Sunnah al-Khas) by analyzing the Prophet's hair management during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The Imam explains that the Prophet preserved his hair not as a ritual requirement, but in anticipation of the divine vision in Surah Al-Fath that he would enter the Sacred Mosque, thereby linking his physical state to the fulfillment of that specific promise. This establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence where actions are validated by their contextual alignment with divine intent rather than mere habitual practice.
